title: OpenPike provider catalog
description: Every LLM provider OpenPike knows about: whether it can receive requests, which API formats it speaks, where its API lives and how to authenticate.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, for editors.

$comment.description: Notes for people editing the file.

providers.description: One entry per provider. Slugs are unique.

format.description: An API format: chat (OpenAI Chat Completions, /v1/chat/completions), messages (Anthropic Messages, /v1/messages), systemone (TypeSafe System One, /v1/systemone).

slug.description: The provider part of a model name, as in <slug>/<model id>.

tier.description: How much work the provider needs: native (first-class), openai-compatible (works through the OpenAI-compatible adapter), special (needs its own sign-in or adapter), planned, or excluded (does not serve chat models).

enabled.description: True when the provider may receive requests (if it is also verified and has adapter, baseUrl, formats and auth).

adapter.description: The gateway adapter that talks to the provider.

baseUrl.description: API base URL, without a trailing slash, from the provider's own documentation. null while it is not known yet (then verify is true).

formats.description: API formats the provider serves natively.

auth.description: How the provider key is sent: Authorization: Bearer, or an x-api-key header.

verify.description: True while the base URL is unconfirmed. The provider stays disabled until a live request succeeds, whatever enabled says.

messagesBaseUrl.description: Base URL of an Anthropic-compatible endpoint, for a provider that is not Anthropic but also serves the messages format.

messagesVerify.description: True while messagesBaseUrl is unconfirmed: the messages format stays off until a live request succeeds.

rejectsStreamOptions.description: True when the provider rejects stream_options, so the gateway does not send it.

notes.description: Free text for people reading the catalog.

liveTested.description: Per format, the last date (YYYY-MM-DD) that format passed OpenPike's live test against the real provider.
